html:
"Positive progress" was reported in indirect discussions between the United States and Iran, even as Tehran issued stark warnings regarding the Strait of Hormuz and prepares for a multi-day state funeral for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, an event poised to be a significant demonstration of national strength.

Russia-Ukraine: A "most massive" Russian attack on Kyiv killed at least 27 people across a wide area, prompting Ukraine to vow retaliation, according to Zelenskyy. Separately, German prosecutors accused Ukraine of ordering the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, and a Ukrainian national has been charged in Germany.

US Diplomacy & Trade: Beyond the Iran talks, the United States is also engaging with artificial intelligence companies, with OpenAI reportedly in early talks to give a 5% stake to the US government as companies attempt to smooth relations with Donald Trump’s administration. Meanwhile, the European Union has moved to target Chinese imports by ending a customs exemption for low-value goods, while also agreeing with Beijing to monitor trade flows and improve access to rare earth materials.

UK Political Transition: Andy Burnham is widely expected to become the next prime minister and has promised to ease cost of living pressures, including potentially reducing business rates and de-privatizing water and energy companies. These plans come amidst an analysis suggesting that Keir Starmer’s decision to cut infrastructure spending to boost defense equipment will cost the UK 10,000 jobs. Additionally, Lisa Nandy announced her department would stop using X, citing concerns over "abuse and misinformation."

Middle East Security & Humanitarian Crises: Allegations of war crimes committed by an Australian citizen serving in the Israel Defense Forces in Gaza, including the deliberate targeting of residential buildings, are being assessed by Australian federal police. Israeli drone attacks wounded people in southern and central Gaza, where breast cancer patients reportedly face immediate mastectomies amid a devastated health sector. Separately, a bomb blast at a Damascus cafe killed at least six, close to a major government building, with no immediate claim of responsibility.

Global Economy & Other Developments: Germany unveiled a sweeping reform push encompassing tax cuts, pension overhauls, and new sick leave rules, with officials cracking down on "exorbitant" sick leave. Elsewhere, the Vatican excommunicated followers and bishops of the Society of Saint Pius X, a traditionalist Catholic sect, after they consecrated bishops without Pope Leo's consent, marking what some observers call a "major crisis." The global cocoa market is also facing a crisis as prices plummeted by nearly 75%, financially crushing West African farmers.
